title: Microglia-derived extracellular vesicle content as a biomarker for early detection of Alzheimer’s disease
title_zh: 微胶质细胞来源的细胞外囊泡成分作为早期阿尔茨海默病检测的生物标志物
abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by amyloid-beta aggregation, tau pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and neuronal loss. While current biomarker frameworks such as the A/T/N classification have advanced diagnosis, they predominantly reflect relatively late stages of disease, limiting opportunities for early intervention. This underscores the urgent need for biomarkers that are not only accessible and sensitive but also specific to the earliest pathogenic mechanisms of AD. Recent work has underscored the pivotal role of disease-associated microglia (DAM) in the onset and progression of AD. DAM exhibit dual roles: they promote protection by phagocytosing amyloid and debris, metabolizing lipids, and remodelling synapses, yet can also drive pathology through excessive cytokine release, chronic inflammatory signalling, and impaired aggregate clearance. DAM release extracellular vesicles (EVs) that encapsulate proteins, nucleic acids, and lipids, reflective of their state. These vesicles reflect microglial (dys)function and can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid and blood, offering a minimally invasive means to monitor early AD pathology. In this review, we examine the emerging evidence that the content of microglia-derived EVs may fulfil the criteria of ideal biomarkers with a focus on the detectability, sensitivity, specificity, and feasibility for longitudinal monitoring. We discuss their potential to overcome limitations of current fluid and imaging biomarkers by offering more stable cargo protection, cell-type specificity, and accessibility in peripheral fluids. Furthermore, we highlight the opportunities and challenges in isolating microglia-derived EVs, identifying reliable surface and cargo markers, and standardizing methodologies for reproducibility across studies. By integrating insights from microglial biology with EV research, we provide evidence for microglia-derived EV content as biomarkers for early detection of AD and propose a roadmap toward DAM-specific EV signatures that could transform early AD diagnosis and disease monitoring. Such advances hold promise not only for AD but also for broader applications in neurodegenerative and neuroinflammatory disorders.
abstract_zh: 摘要 阿尔茨海默病（AD）是一种进行性神经退行性疾病，特征为淀粉样β聚集、tau病理、突触功能障碍和神经元损失。当前的生物标志物框架，如A/T/N分类，已推动诊断进展，但主要反映疾病相对晚期阶段，限制了早期干预的机会。这凸显了迫切需要既可获取、敏感又特异于AD最早致病机制的生物标志物。近期研究强调了与疾病相关的微胶质细胞（DAM）在AD发病和进展中的关键作用。DAM具有双重功能：它们通过吞噬淀粉样蛋白和碎片、代谢脂质以及重塑突触来促进保护，但也可能通过过度细胞因子释放、慢性炎症信号和聚集物清除受损来驱动病理。DAM释放的细胞外囊泡（EV）封装了蛋白质、核酸和脂质，反映其状态。这些囊泡反映微胶质细胞的（失）功能，可在脑脊液和血液中检测，为监测早期AD病理提供了一种微创手段。本文综述了微胶质细胞来源的EV成分可能满足理想生物标志物标准的最新证据，重点关注其可检测性、敏感性、特异性和纵向监测的可行性。我们讨论了它们通过提供更稳定的载荷保护、细胞类型特异性以及在外周液体中的可获取性，克服当前体液和影像生物标志物局限性的潜力。此外，我们强调了分离微胶质细胞来源EV、识别可靠表面和载荷标记以及标准化方法以实现跨研究可重复性的机遇与挑战。通过整合微胶质细胞生物学与EV研究的见解，我们提供了微胶质细胞来源EV成分作为早期AD检测生物标志物的证据，并提出了通向DAM特异性EV签名的路线图，可能改变早期AD诊断和疾病监测。这些进展不仅对AD具有前景，也对更广泛的神经退行性和神经炎症疾病具有应用价值。
